clue.text: The majesty of King George under a madness?

indicators.note: madness suggests a crazed, disordered state, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George's royal cipher
taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A question about whether a mad King George, such as George III, still kept his royal dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' looks like a position word placing one piece below another, but it is plain fodder for the anagram along with 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is impressive splendour and dignity, a close synonym for the stateliness of royalty.

clue.text: Snakes and serpents possess small heads

indicators.note: heads are the front ends, so only the opening letter of each word is wanted

blocks.note: the opening letter of and
the opening letter of serpents
the opening letter of possess
the opening letter of small

explanation.surface: A naturalist's observation that snakes have tiny heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small heads' reads as a description of snakes, but 'heads' tells you to take the first letters of the four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous Egyptian vipers, so they are one kind of snake, the one that killed Cleopatra.

clue.text: Bear last seen by Yorkshire river

blocks.note: the last part of something is its end
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A bear was spotted for the last time beside a river in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning to put up with something.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear hardship is to tolerate or withstand it, which is what enduring means.

clue.text: Flower left out when Bastille collapsed

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so a letter standing for left is removed from the word
a collapsed building falls into a jumbled heap, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
the Paris fortress, taken as written

explanation.surface: A flower was abandoned when the Bastille fell in the French Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Ls in Bastille is dropped, and the seven letters left are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Astilbe is a garden perennial with feathery plumes of tiny blooms, an example of a flowering plant.

clue.text: Busy worker getting disgruntled is given reinforcement

blocks.note: a worker bee is proverbially busy
being fed up is feeling disgruntled

explanation.surface: An overworked employee grows unhappy and is sent extra staff to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy worker' sounds like a human employee; in crosswords it is usually the bee.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beefed up has been strengthened or bolstered, the same as having had reinforcement added.

clue.text: Mark on tongue seen before a fever

blocks.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
a tongue is a language, here Latin
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor notices a spot on a patient's tongue just before a fever develops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' suggests the body part, especially next to 'fever', but it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlatina is another name for scarlet fever, the illness with a red rash.

clue.text: French cheeses, so people say, produce slight wind

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so it is the pronunciation of the cheeses that matters

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese, here in the plural

explanation.surface: A joke that rich French cheeses cause flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on wind as flatulence; the answer is the gentle weather sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is a gentle current of air, a mild version of the weather word for moving air.

clue.text: Reporters besieging network for handouts

indicators.note: an army besieging a town surrounds it, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: the press is the collective term for reporters
read as net-work: the word net, worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Journalists crowd round a television network in search of free material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'network' looks like one word, but the setter splits it: net is the fodder and work tells you to rework it.
explanation.definitionFit: Presents are gifts handed out to people, so handouts in the sense of free gifts.

clue.text: Call for Sargent, say, before a sergeant, say, entered

indicators.note: something that has entered is now inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: ere is an old word for before
a sergeant is an example of a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A muddled-looking note about a sergeant marching in ahead of someone named Sargent.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Malcolm Sargent was a famous British conductor, so the call is an audience's demand for more. The near-identical Sargent and sergeant are deliberate.
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is the audience's shout asking a performer, such as a conductor, to come back and play again.

clue.text: Responsibility for extra payment not being introduced

indicators.note: a word not introduced has lost its opening, so its first letter is removed

blocks.note: a bonus is a payment on top of normal wages

explanation.surface: Someone is held accountable for a bonus that was never brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: BONUS loses its first letter B to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The onus is the duty or burden that falls on a person, a formal word for responsibility.

clue.text: Ignorant about naval leader not being in mufti

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is taken
about means around, so one piece is placed round the other

blocks.note: the opening letter of naval
mufti is civilian clothes, so someone not in mufti is wearing uniform

explanation.surface: A naval officer in uniform is accused of not knowing what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: Mufti is the old military word for civilian dress worn off duty. N goes inside UNIFORMED after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uninformed lacks knowledge or information, which is exactly being ignorant of something.

clue.text: Secure, resettled and free

indicators.note: resettled means placed again in a new position, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Refugees made safe, moved to a new home and at liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secure' looks like the first of three adjectives, but it is the word whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to set them loose from danger or captivity, so free as a verb.

clue.text: Glowing tin going down

blocks.note: a tin is a can
a descent is a movement downwards

explanation.surface: Molten tin flowing downwards with a bright glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin' reads as the metal, which suits glowing; here it is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Candescent describes something shining with white heat, a rarer form of incandescent.

clue.text: College servant putting foreign currency in mug

indicators.note: in places one thing within another, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a beaker is a drinking cup or mug
DM is the Deutschmark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A servant at a college slipping some foreign money into a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: At Cambridge colleges a bedmaker, or bedder, cleans students' rooms. The Deutschmark was Germany's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedmaker is the domestic worker employed by a Cambridge college to tidy undergraduates' rooms.

clue.text: £1,000 annually for a family member

blocks.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
p.a. is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: An allowance of a thousand pounds a year paid to a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandpa is an informal name for a grandfather, one of the relatives in a family.

clue.text: Animal enclosed by some low walls

indicators.note: something enclosed is shut inside, so the first piece goes within the second

blocks.note: some of a thing is parts of it
an ape is an animal

explanation.surface: A creature penned in by a few low walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' looks like a quantity word qualifying the walls, but it is the outer piece of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Parapets are low protective walls along the edge of a roof, bridge or balcony.

clue.text: Elastic band held by agent

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: a secret agent is a spy
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A secret agent keeping a rubber band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elastic band' reads as one object; the split comes between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something springy bounces back into shape after being stretched or pressed, like an elastic material.

clue.text: Conveying rage and lust using sign language?

indicators.note: conveying means carrying or moving, so the letters are moved about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone expressing fury and desire without words, through gestures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conveying' reads as expressing feelings, but it signals the rearrangement. The question mark admits that the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestural means relating to or made by gestures, and sign language communicates through hand gestures.

clue.text: Some colleges say education is tried

indicators.note: some means a part only, so the answer is a stretch of the following letters

blocks.note: found running through the end of the first word, all of the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Certain colleges claim that education has been put to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is a formal old word for attempting it, so essayed means attempted.

clue.text: Auditor brought into companies supplying weapons

indicators.note: something brought into a place ends up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: firms are business companies
an auditor is a listener, and the ear is what hears

explanation.surface: An accountant is called in to inspect companies that sell arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant; literally it means a hearer, hence the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Firearms are guns, the portable weapons fired with gunpowder.

clue.text: Decapitated clergyman - American aviation casualty long ago

indicators.note: decapitated means beheaded, so the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: a vicar is a parish clergyman
US is the abbreviation for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: A headless priest and an American airman killed in an early flying accident.
explanation.walkthrough: VICAR loses its V. The 'aviation casualty' is from Greek myth, not aviation history.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth Icarus flew on wax wings too near the sun and fell to his death, the first flier lost.

clue.text: Santa Fe's last article

indicators.note: last points to the final position, so only the closing letter is taken

blocks.note: Santa Claus is Father Christmas
the closing letter of Fe

explanation.surface: The final item about Santa Fe, the city in New Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Santa Fe' reads as one place name; split it into Santa and Fe.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause is a numbered section in a legal document, also called an article.

clue.text: Letter from Greece to New Zealand about tiptop material

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
NZ is the abbreviation for New Zealand
read as tip-top, the top of tip, which is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Sending a Greek letter to New Zealand about some first-rate fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiptop' looks like one word meaning excellent; it is read as the top of 'tip'. T goes inside NZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Chintz is a glazed printed cotton fabric, often flowery, used for curtains and upholstery.

clue.text: Stone coffins transported in a cargo ship

indicators.note: transported means carried off somewhere else, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Ancient stone coffins shipped as freight on a cargo vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcophagi are carved stone burial chests, such as those of Egyptian pharaohs; this is the Latin plural.

clue.text: Small sweet potato

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
pud is British slang for pudding, a sweet course

explanation.surface: A little sweet potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet potato' is a real vegetable, but the definition is 'potato' alone; 'sweet' means dessert, which British speakers call pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is the informal, homely slang name for the everyday tuber used for chips and mash.

clue.text: Resentful god overthrown

indicators.note: something overthrown is turned upside down, which in a down entry turns the word end over end

blocks.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: A deity bitter at being toppled from power.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sore about something means being aggrieved or upset by it, a colloquial sense of resentful.

clue.text: Boat carrying empty Norse basket

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only its outside letters
carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed boat pushed with a pole
the outside letters of Norse

explanation.surface: A Viking boat carrying an empty basket.
explanation.walkthrough: A punt is the flat boat poled along rivers at Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A punnet is a small square container or basket in which strawberries and other soft fruit are sold.

clue.text: Everlasting kiss inside or outside

indicators.note: inside places the first item within the next one

blocks.note: eternal means lasting for ever
X is the conventional sign for a kiss

explanation.surface: A romantic wondering whether an undying kiss belongs indoors or out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' and 'outside' look like a pair of alternatives, but the first is the instruction and the second the definition. X goes in after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: External means on the exterior or outer surface of something, the opposite of internal.
